A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fine-R1 and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original content can be matched reliably despite the new appendix and subsequent renumbering in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original FGVR experiments, ablations, representation analyses and general-capability evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments applying CoT SFT and TAPO to openPangu-VL-7B in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The structured CoT SFT procedure, intra-class and inter-class augmentations, and TAPO objective remain unchanged. Appendix F applies the existing pipeline to another backbone without documenting an algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six FGVR datasets and ImageWikiQA, MME, MMBench and SEED-Bench. The added openPangu experiment reuses the existing FGVR tasks and seen/unseen-category evaluation.

E2.justification: New Table 7 adds zero-shot openPangu-VL-7B and its CoT-SFT-only variant as comparators for the openPangu-based pipeline. Existing CLIP, general/reasoning MLLM and Qwen2-VL DAPO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds an openPangu-VL-7B evaluation configuration with zero-shot, CoT SFT and CoT SFT+TAPO variants, reporting closed-world accuracy. Existing experiments retain their stated category splits, four-shot setup, metrics and training settings.

E4.justification: v3 extends the cross-model generalization analysis beyond Qwen and compares CoT SFT with CoT SFT+TAPO on openPangu. The existing component ablations, sensitivity analyses, representation analyses and qualitative cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: New Table 7 follows the existing practice of averaging three trials without reporting dispersion or confidence intervals. Previously stated trial counts and Table 4's statistical reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports openPangu overall accuracies of 71.82% for zero-shot, 82.80% for CoT SFT and 82.90% for CoT SFT+TAPO. The corresponding unseen averages are 66.77%, 79.76% and 79.54%. Previously reported results, including v1 Table 7 renumbered as v3 Table 8, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(5), including the TAPO objective and relative semantic similarity, are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about four-shot FGVR performance, unseen-category generalization and improved deployment of existing knowledge. The additional experiment supplies supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F reiterates the existing cross-model generality interpretation using openPangu results. The knowledge-deployment explanation in Section 5.4 and the general-capability and qualitative interpretations remain unchanged; no new mechanism or limitation is articulated.

D1.justification: The prompt templates, implementation hyperparameters, hardware disclosure and code-access statement are unchanged. The new appendix identifies openPangu-VL-7B but supplies no additional model-specific implementation instructions or training details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Peng et al.'s survey of fine-grained MLLMs, Zhang et al.'s FGM-SPCL work and Luo et al.'s openPangu quantization work. These are limited citation additions; the overall positioning against prior approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: A short new Appendix F is inserted, shifting the former Appendices F-H to G-I and updating cross-references. Local wording and citation-format edits accompany it, while the main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 7 and renumbers the previous general-capability table as Table 8. Appendix reflow places the unchanged Figure 6 before its explanatory section on the following page. Existing figures are retained without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix F modestly strengthens empirical validation by testing the pipeline beyond the Qwen family. Table 7 shows a substantial improvement over zero-shot openPangu, but nearly all comes from CoT SFT: TAPO adds only 0.10 percentage points overall and lowers unseen accuracy from 79.76% to 79.54%. The absence of uncertainty estimates and a DAPO control limits the additional evidence for TAPO specifically. The original evidence remains intact.
